articles.title: Air Canada cancels all flights to U.S. state due to low demand
articles.summary: The national airline initially entered the market with a flight from Toronto in 2001.
articles.body:
While the number of Canadians going to the U.S. for leisure trips saw a small bounceback over several months last summer, cross-border travel is still at a low unseen in decades driven above all by President Donald Trump's aggressive rhetoric and politics toward the northern neighbor.

According to the monthly numbers published by the Canadian government's statistics agency, the number of Canadian trips to the U.S. in September 2026 was down by 29% compared to two years ago in 2024 — a 31% decrease for car border crossings and a 19% drop for flights.

Air Canada to permanently cut flight to South Carolina in 2027

Airlines have, in turn, responded to the weaker demand by cutting routes to smaller cities that once served a market but now do not bring in enough sold seats.

Air Canada was already scheduled to phase out its routes from Minneapolis and Detroit from Montreal and Indianapolis from Toronto by the end of October. The national airline is now reported to not be bringing back its flight to Charleston International Airport (CHS) from Toronto Pearson (YYZ) for 2027.

As a seasonal route that began in March and last year ended at the start of September, the Toronto-Charleston flight was first launched in 2001 and brought back for the summer of 2024 after being retired during the Covid-19 pandemic.

It was, at the time of launch, the first direct flight to Charleston from outside of the United States. Over the years, it has served both business travelers going between the two cities and the growing travel interest in the city from Canada.

As Toronto was Air Canada's only flight into Charleston, the decision not to bring back the seasonal route marks a market exit from the city and the state of South Carolina.

'We have made the decision to discontinue:' Air Canada on axed Charleston-Toronto flight

According to the analysis from aviation website Simple Flying, the 200 departures and 15,200 seats flown from Toronto in 2024 dropped to just 92 departures and 6,992 seats flown following Trump's Canadian tariffs and repeated comments about making Canada a 51st state in 2025.

As such, Air Canada made the business decision to not bring back the route.

Without commenting on the reasons for the abrupt dropoff in travel numbers, an Air Canada representative confirmed the suspension of the seasonal flight. They said that, above all, its flight network is determined by where its customers are shown to be purchasing tickets.

articles.title: Frango pode ficar mais barato, principalmente no Sul, após caso de Newcastle em SC, diz Itaú | G1
articles.standfirst: China, Arábia Saudita, Chile e México suspenderam as compras de frango de Santa Catarina após a confirmação do foco da doença, o que pode aumentar a oferta no mercado brasileiro e reduzir os preços no atacado.
articles.summary: China, Arábia Saudita, Chile e México suspenderam as compras de frango de Santa Catarina após a confirmação do foco da doença, o que pode aumentar a oferta no mercado brasileiro e reduzir os preços no atacado.
articles.body:
Frango pode ficar mais barato, principalmente no Sul, após caso de Newcastle em SC, diz Itaú — Foto: Claudio Schwarz/Unplash

O frango pode ficar mais barato nos próximos meses, principalmente na Região Sul do Brasil, após a confirmação de um foco da doença de Newcastle em Nova Itaberaba, em Santa Catarina , avalia o banco Itaú BBA, em relatório divulgado nesta sexta-feira (23).

O efeito deve ser mais perceptível no atacado e pode se intensificar no primeiro trimestre de 2027, quando a procura dos consumidores costuma diminuir, diz o banco.

Na prévia da inflação de outubro , também divulgada nesta sexta-feira, o frango em pedaços ficou 0,71% mais caro no mês. Em 12 meses, porém, o preço acumula queda de 4%, segundo o Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

🔍A DNC é uma doença viral que afeta aves domésticas e silvestres . Em quadros graves, pode causar problemas respiratórios e neurológicos em aves. Em humanos, a infecção é rara e geralmente leve, podendo provocar conjuntivite temporária após contato direto com aves infectadas ou suas secreções; não há transmissão da doença pelo consumo de frango.

A possibilidade de queda nos preços está ligada à suspensão das exportações de frango de Santa Catarina. China, Arábia Saudita, Chile e México , que estão entre os compradores do produto catarinense, anunciaram nesta semana que vão deixar de importar a carne produzida no estado.

Santa Catarina está particularmente exposta porque exporta cerca de 63% do frango que produz , a maior proporção entre os estados brasileiros. Na média nacional, 37% da produção é destinada ao exterior.

Com menos destinos disponíveis, frigoríficos catarinenses podem ter de vender no país parte da produção que seria enviada ao exterior. Isso tende a aumentar a oferta, principalmente na Região Sul, e pode levar as empresas a reduzir os preços para conseguir vender o excedente.

Segundo o Itaú BBA, os frigoríficos também podem enfrentar acúmulo de estoques, aumento dos gastos com armazenagem e logística e maior pressão sobre o caixa.

Por que os preços podem cair após a virada do ano

A possível entrada de mais frango no mercado interno ocorre em um momento em que a produção já está crescendo.

De janeiro a setembro, foram abatidas 3,7% mais aves do que no mesmo período de 2025. Já a quantidade de carne produzida cresceu ainda mais, 6,2%, segundo estimativas do Itaú BBA. Para o ano inteiro, o banco espera que a produção avance cerca de 6%.

Até agora, esse aumento da produção não derrubou os preços porque as exportações continuaram fortes e ajudaram a retirar parte do frango do mercado brasileiro. Além disso, como a ave segue mais barata que a carne bovina, muitos consumidores optam pelo frango, o que mantém a procura aquecida e dá sustentação aos preços.

Esse equilíbrio, porém, pode mudar na virada do ano. Com as restrições às exportações, parte do frango que seria vendida a outros países pode ficar no Brasil, aumentando ainda mais a quantidade disponível.

Ao mesmo tempo, o consumo costuma diminuir depois das festas, quando acaba o dinheiro extra do 13º salário e despesas como impostos, matrícula e material escolar passam a pesar no orçamento das famílias.

Com mais frango disponível e menos pessoas comprando, os preços podem cair, principalmente no atacado da Região Sul. Isso não significa, porém, que o produto necessariamente ficará mais barato nos supermercados, pondera o Itaú.

Isso porque, mesmo que os frigoríficos reduzam o valor cobrado do atacado, o varejo pode não repassar integralmente esse desconto ao consumidor. O preço nos supermercados também inclui custos de transporte, armazenamento e comercialização.

O Itaú ressalta ainda que o impacto sobre os preços dependerá, principalmente, de quanto tempo os países levarão para voltar a comprar o frango catarinense.

Em 2024, por exemplo, após um foco da doença de Newcastle no Rio Grande do Sul, a redução das exportações ficou concentrada em apenas um mês e os preços não caíram. Já em 2025, as restrições adotadas depois de um caso de gripe aviária foram mais amplas e duraram cerca de quatro meses, período em que os preços desaceleraram.

Para o Itaú BBA, o episódio atual deve ficar entre os dois casos, com impacto concentrado em Santa Catarina e no atacado da Região Sul.

articles.title: Volvo Cars shares plunge on losses, job cuts
articles.summary: Shares in Swedish carmaker Volvo Cars plunged Friday after it said US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarte...
articles.body:
Shares in Swedish carmaker Volvo Cars plunged Friday after it said US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarter loss.

The company also said it would cut about 2,500 jobs worldwide.

Volvo Cars, controlled by Chinese group Geely, reported revenue of 66.9 billion kronor ($6.7 billion) for the third quarter, down nearly 23 percent from the same period last year.

It swung to a net loss of 5.7 billion kronor for the quarter from a net profit of 4.5 billion kronor a year earlier.

Around 1000 GMT, Volvo Cars shares were down over 25 percent on the Stockholm stock exchange.

"We continue to operate in a very tough environment with strong external challenges: de-globalisation, hypercompetition and climate change," chief executive Hakan Samuelsson said in a statement.

In response, the company announced a new five-billion-kronor savings plan it said would lead to about 2,000 job cuts in Sweden and 500 more globally, "through natural attrition and by targeted exit packages to employees".

The company currently employs some 39,300 people worldwide, including 19,500 in Sweden, it said in an email to AFP.

The company, which had bet heavily on electric vehicles, said the removal of consumer incentives for EVs in the United States under President Donald Trump had also hit its margins.

In 2024, Volvo Cars dropped a plan to transition to exclusively EV sales by the end of the decade.

"We are convinced that we have the right long-term strategy addressing these challenges," Samuelsson said.

"However, in the short term, with severely challenged volumes, we need to reinforce our turnaround plan with additional decisive actions, lowering our break-even point and improving cash flows to make us more resilient."

Struggling along with other European auto companies in the face of a difficult global landscape, Volvo Cars last year announced an 18-billion-kronor cost-cutting plan.

In May 2025, the group said it would cut 3,000 jobs and two years earlier, 1,300 positions in Sweden were eliminated.

Calling the third quarter "very disappointing", Samuelsson said the company was struggling in particular in the US and Chinese markets.

In China, the market for "legacy premium brands is in severe decline due to intense competition from new Chinese alternatives, basically eliminating profitability for legacy premium brands," the chief executive said.

The situation led to a nearly 50 percent drop in revenue in China compared to a year earlier.

articles.title: Apple is taking Wall Street's top spot back from Nvidia — for the fifth time
articles.summary: Apple briefly topped Nvidia in market value Friday, a move it has made before that has rarely stuck.
articles.body:
Apple ( AAPL ) is taking Wall Street's crown back from Nvidia — for the fifth time.

Apple briefly topped Nvidia in market value on Friday. It's a move Apple has made before, and it has rarely stuck.

Apple and Nvidia ( NVDA ) are each worth about $5.1 trillion, and the gap between them was less than 1% at Thursday's close. The flip came alongside a record run for Apple's stock and the day the tech giant's $1,999 iPhone Duo hit stores , capping a battle investors had been watching all morning. Nvidia has since moved back into the lead.

For most of the past decade, this wasn't much of a contest. Apple closed as the most valuable US-listed company in about 7 of every 10 sessions since October 2015. Microsoft ( MSFT ) took the top spot in stretches, Amazon ( AMZN ) held it for 12 sessions in early 2019, and Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) got exactly one day in 2016.

Then the AI boom rewrote the leaderboard.

Nvidia first closed at No. 1 on June 18, 2024. It has held the spot almost without a break since June 2025, interrupted only by a four-session Apple run in late July.

Apple has reclaimed the crown from Nvidia four times before today. Only once did it last, when the DeepSeek scare sank chip stocks in January 2025 and Apple held on into the spring.

Since the start of 2024, the No. 1 spot has changed hands two dozen times, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

This time, the two stocks are heading in opposite directions. Apple closed Thursday at a record. Nvidia sits about 11% below its Oct. 6 record close after this month's chip rout .

Since that Oct. 6 close, which was also the S&P 500's ( ^IXIC ) record, Apple is the only megacap stock in the green. It's up 4%.

Watch whether Apple can finish the day on top. It hasn't since July 30.

The next big test comes on Wednesday, when Microsoft and Alphabet report earnings. They rank third and fourth, each worth about $3.9 trillion.

articles.title: US consumer sentiment near record low ahead of midterm elections
articles.summary: By Dan Burns Oct 23 (Reuters) - US consumer sentiment edged down to near a record low in October as rising prices because of the Middle East conflict soured...
articles.body:
Oct 23 (Reuters) - US consumer sentiment edged down to near a record low in October as rising prices because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy on the doorstep of midterm congressional elections centering on affordability issues, a survey showed ‌on Friday.

The University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers said its Consumer Sentiment Index dropped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in ‌September. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the index at 46.3, which had also been the index's preliminary reading for October.

October's reading marked the second-lowest on record after the all-time low of 44.8 set ​in May, not long after the Iran war began.

"Purchasing power continues to dominate consumer views of the economy," said Joanne Hsu, the director of the Surveys of Consumers. "Sentiment is now 10% below a year ago and 15% less than February, just prior to the Iran conflict."

The survey results dovetail with political polling data showing voters have a dim view of the economy and President Donald Trump's and the Republican Party's stewardship over it.

Millions of US voters have already cast early ballots in the fast-approaching November 3 midterm election ‌that will determine control of Congress over the final ⁠two years of Trump's term. Polls show Republicans are likely to lose control of the House of Representatives and possibly the Senate as Trump's approval rating in a Reuters/Ipsos poll sits at a record low thanks to the skyrocketing fuel prices unleashed by his ⁠decision to attack Iran in late February.

University of Michigan data broken down by political party affiliation showed the weaker sentiment was led by survey respondents self-identified as independents, who comprise a critical bloc of swing voters. Their sentiment score dropped to 42.4 — just above May's record-low 40.6 — from 47.7 in September, while scores for Democrats and Republicans improved.

The survey showed a ​significant ​upswing this year among independents — and also notably Republicans — citing high prices as a drag on ​their personal finances. Since January, the number of independents referencing ‌inflation pressures as hurting their financial situation rose by 27%, while it has shot up by 52% among Republicans. Similar citations among Democrats, meanwhile, are up by 15%.

Households with no or limited exposure to the stock market — until recently climbing rapidly on enthusiasm for the artificial intelligence investment boom — also have cited high prices as a drag on their finances more frequently than at the start of the year.

articles.title: Your forgotten retirement account could be costing you money
articles.summary: Forgotten IRAs could be quietly draining your retirement savings. Here are a few tips to find your lost accounts, plus expert advice on making a plan for you...
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

Starting a new job can be an exciting time, and for many people, it's easy to forget about the employer-sponsored retirement account they left behind.

Capitalize, a company that helps people roll over retirement accounts, estimates that 31.9 million 401(k) accounts were left behind or forgotten as of July 2025. Those accounts hold about $2.1 trillion in assets, up almost 30% from mid-2023. The firm says the number of forgotten 401(k)s has almost doubled over the last decade.

Even if people haven't really forgotten about these accounts, doing nothing can still cost them. When 401(k)s are left alone, and the balance is small, that money is sometimes automatically rolled over into an IRA. That can come with several drawbacks, such as hidden fees and limited investment options that may not align with your overall retirement plan.

"The biggest mistake is just never deciding," said David Talley, CFP® at Talley Wealth. "People change jobs, the old 401(k) sits there, and nobody's thinking about what those dollars are for anymore."

What happens to your 401(k) balance when you leave a job?

When you leave an employer, you have a few different options to choose from regarding your retirement account.

Employees with a smaller balance of under $1,000 may automatically be sent a check. Those with a larger balance can still opt to cash out, though this is typically not recommended, as it may incur taxes and penalties for those under age 59½.

Workers can also roll over their 401(k) or 403(b) into an individual retirement account (IRA) at a brokerage.

Alternatively, many workers choose to roll over their 401(k) or 403(b) into their new employer's plan to keep their retirement savings all under one roof. Some employees choose to leave their money where it is, and as long as your balance is over $7,000, most plans allow you to keep your money invested.

Employees with balances of more than $1,000 and up to $7,000 may have those funds automatically rolled over by their plan administrator into a "safe harbor" IRA without that former employee's consent.

This is where choosing the path of least resistance can lead to losing money over time.

How neglecting an old 401(k) can affect your retirement savings

According to a white paper from PensionBee, a retirement provider that offers IRAs, using data from the Employee Benefit Research Institute (EBRI), the number of automatic rollovers is projected to double from 1.1 million per year in 2022 to 2.2 million annually in 2030. By then, an estimated 13 million accounts holding roughly $43 billion in retirement savings could be sitting in safe harbor IRAs, the paper estimates.

The concern with allowing those funds to be automatically rolled over without understanding the terms and conditions of the automatic IRA is that workers could be hindering their own retirement savings progress.

Unlike traditional IRAs, which allow you to invest your funds in practically any stocks, bonds, or funds you choose, safe harbor IRAs are typically ultra-low-risk money market funds that have minimal returns and may come with a number of fees that eat into your balance. The white paper suggests that the longer an account stays in an automatic rollover IRA, the more likely it is to decline in value after one year. After eight years, 4 in 10 accounts were worth less than when they arrived, according to the white paper.

Talley says another common mistake people make with their old 401(k) accounts is cashing out because the balance feels small, and paying tax, and usually a penalty, on money that was supposed to be for retirement.

"The third is rolling everything to an IRA on autopilot without looking at what the old plan or the new one actually does well," Talley said.

If you suspect you have forgotten retirement savings floating around, contact the human resources department at your old employer(s) for the plan administrator information.

Once you track down your money, you can leave it where it is, cash it out if it makes sense for your financial plan, roll it over into an IRA, or roll it over into your current employer's plan.

"Find out what it's invested in and what it's costing you, and then make a decision about it, even if the decision is to leave it alone," Talley said.

articles.title: Coforge revenue grew 40% in Q2; margin guidance raised to 16%
articles.summary: Coforge Q2 revenue jumps 40% YoY to $652.2M; operating margin at 16%. FY27 margin guidance raised to 16% as order book hits $2.38B.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Coforge’s revenue rose 40.1% year on year and 10.1% sequentially in dollar terms to $652.2 million in the September quarter. Organic revenue growth in constant currency (CC) terms was 3.8% sequentially.Operating margin expanded 134 basis points year on year to 16%, while remaining flat sequentially.The company raised its FY27 operating margin guidance to 16% from 15.5% and expects to expand it further to 17% next year.“The 10.1% sequential growth and 40.1% YoY growth in US dollar terms, a 3.8% sequential organic CC growth, a next twelve month signed order book of $2.38 billion, an order intake of over $1 billion and eight large deals, the most the firm has ever signed in a single quarter, have put us firmly on course to be the industry growth leader for the third year running,” said Coforge CEO Sudhir Singh.Order intake stood at $1 billion, while the executable order book for the next 12 months rose 45.4% year on year to $2.38 billion. The company signed eight large deals during the quarter.“We are raising our FY27 EBIT margin guidance from 15.5% to 16%. We expect to further improve our EBIT margin to 17% next year; and will be targeting to be among top three scaled IT services firms on margins while maintaining our growth momentum,” Singh said.The Americas accounted for 63.1% of revenue, followed by Europe, the Middle East and Africa at 24.6% and the rest of the world at 12.3%. Banking, financial services and insurance contributed 25.3% of revenue, while healthcare and high-tech accounted for 17.6%.Coforge’s headcount rose to 47,365 from 46,228 in the previous quarter. Attrition stood at 10.4% on a last-twelve-month basis, excluding its business process services workforce.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: The AI sell-off is crushing stocks of companies leading the data center build-out
articles.summary: Bloom Energy and Comfort Systems just posted blowout quarters, and Wall Street is dumping their stocks anyway as the AI data center trade cracks.
articles.body:
Two of the AI building boom's biggest suppliers just posted blowout quarters. Wall Street is dumping them anyway.

Bloom Energy ( BE ), whose fuel cells generate power on-site at data centers, said Thursday that sales jumped 138% last quarter and raised its full-year outlook to roughly 122% growth. Comfort Systems ( FIX ), which installs the cooling and electrical systems inside them, said its backlog nearly doubled to $17.8 billion.

Both stocks are falling hard for a second straight day. Credo ( CRDO ), which makes networking parts for data centers, is sliding with them.

"A company can deliver extraordinary numbers, but if investors aren't willing to reward those results, something isn't right," Steve Strazza of All Star Charts wrote Friday morning .

Bloom did give the bears something to chew on. Its cash flow turned negative in the quarter, and its margins aren't keeping pace with sales.

Since the S&P 500's ( ^IXIC ) Oct. 6 record close, the companies building and equipping AI data centers are down a median 23%, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. That group includes heavyweights like Caterpillar ( CAT ), GE Vernova ( GEV ), Vertiv ( VRT ), and Eaton ( ETN ).

Power producers are down 14%. Nvidia ( NVDA ) is off 11%. The Big Tech companies writing the checks are down just 5%.

In other words, the companies cashing the checks are falling harder than the ones writing them.

That's backward for a build-out whose biggest problem is supply. "The biggest constraint right now for the AI build-out is power," Jefferies' Aniket Shah told Yahoo Finance on Wednesday, pointing to public pushback against new data centers . Even Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said builders have to be good neighbors .

Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk wrote this week that demand for computing power is "significantly greater than supply." That means a slower build-out should actually help owners of scarce capacity, he argued, from power producers to transformer makers, where lead times run "up to 26 months." The losers would be "developers and construction-stage investors" and AI stocks priced for everything to arrive on time. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)

The real risk, Sløk wrote, is that "scarcity unwinds" if supply catches up or demand softens. Now even his would-be winners are falling. That's the market betting on the worst case.

Together, a dozen of the biggest builders and power names have shed more than $300 billion in market value since Oct. 6.
